subject: How to estimate prevalence of each geographical area for small area estimation

messages.author: 922cfd50e52024b9
messages.subject: How to estimate prevalence of each geographical area for small area estimation
parts:
Hi!
I'm very new to INLA and Bayesian statistics. I'm trying to estimate prevalence of stunting by districts. I've tried to write some code Can anyone verify my code to estimate prevalence by DISTRICT adjusting for multiple fixed effect variables using INLA package for small area estimation.

Code:
# construct neighbor list from shape files containing polygons
nb <- spdep::poly2nb(regions_shapefile,row.names = regions_shapefile$DISTRICT)

# Construct adjacent matrix
adj_matrix <- spdep::nb2mat(nb, style="B", zero.policy=TRUE)

# Define the INLA model formula
formula <- outcome ~Age+Sex+Rural_urban+ f(DISTRICT, model="besag", graph=adj_matrix,scale.model  = T)


# Fit the model with INLA, including weights
result <- inla(formula,
               family="binomial", weights = hv005/100000,
               control.predictor = list(compute = TRUE),
               control.compute = list(return.marginals.predictor = TRUE),
               data=PRdata2)
               
# Examine results
summary(result)

# Fixed and random effects
fixed_effect <-result$summary.fixed
random_effect<-result$summary.random$DISTRICT

# Estimate prevalence for each districts
prevalence <-exp(random_effect)/(1+exp(random_effect$mean))

messages.author: 3eab71733027a24a
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] How to estimate prevalence of each geographical area for small area estimation
parts:
I guess you have checked the 'nb', as the regions must be 1, 2, ..., n, which is
then also used int he data.frame.

weights = hv005/100000 is not what you want. If you want to state number of
trials, then use 'Ntrials=hv005' (without knowing what 'hv005' is)
